Merge pull request #699 from pwndoc/fix-demo-display

Fix demo display
Usability changes

Restore v-model on the editable Proofs editor

The basic-editor instance in the findings edit Proofs tab lost its
v-model="finding.poc" binding when AI props were added, so content
typed there was never saved. Add a unit test that mounts the real
template (unstubbing the wrapping tab/card/field components) to guard
against silent v-model regressions like this one.

Fix invalid Anthropic default model ID

claude-opus-4.8 is not a valid Anthropic model ID (Anthropic uses
dashes, not dots): claude-opus-4-8. First generation against
Anthropic 404s with no in-UI explanation. openaiModel (gpt-5.4-mini)
and deepseekModel (deepseek-v4-flash) were checked against current
provider catalogs and are valid as-is.

Make AI provider secrets clearable

mergeSettingsSecrets treated any empty incoming value the same as the
masked sentinel, so a user could never remove a stored API key short
of a DB edit. Distinguish "unchanged" (masked sentinel) from
"explicitly cleared" (empty string): masked keeps the existing value,
empty clears it, anything else sets it.

The frontend now resends the masked sentinel for untouched fields
instead of an empty string, so a genuinely emptied field is
unambiguous. Add settings-secrets unit tests and a backend integration
test covering the clear case.

Wire up the outdated audit QA report path

The loadOnly path in handleAiQa used getLatestQaReport, which
hardcoded outdated: false, so the fingerprint comparison never ran and
the UI never showed staleness after editing findings. Switch to
getCachedQaReport/getOutdatedQaReport (already implemented and
tested, but unused) which correctly compute staleness via the audit
content fingerprint. The vulnerability QA load paths already did this
correctly and are unchanged.

Add a dismissible "results are out of date" banner to qa-results-panel
when outdated is true, wired through both the audit QA sidebar (store
state) and the vulnerability QA panel (previously missing "outdated"
from its data(), so it wasn't reactive).

Default AI integration to opt-in (disabled)

ai.public.enabled defaulted to true and ensureInitialized force-set it
to true on upgrade, so every install/upgrade surfaced AI buttons that
fail with a confusing provider error until keys are configured.
Sending report content to a third-party API should be an explicit org
decision. Default enabled to false in both the schema and the
upgrade-initialization path (which still only sets the field when it's
missing, same as before).

Per maintainer guidance, this only flips the enabled default — the
audits:ai-generate/audits:ai-qa core-permission flags are untouched
pending a separate decision, since that changes the default role
matrix.

ai-integration.test.js now explicitly enables AI in its setup instead
of relying on the previous implicit default, since its tests exercise
AI-enabled behavior.

Document the AI QA prompt-injection surface

Audit/finding content is placed in the AI QA model's user payload,
so imported or untrusted content can attempt to steer the AI's
review output. Impact is limited (advisory output only), but it was
previously undocumented. Add a docs note under Data > AI Integration
and strengthen the existing "AI review" caption on AI-sourced QA
issues to read "AI review — verify before acting".

Extend qa-results-panel tests to cover the caption rendering only for
source === 'ai' issues.

Confirm before destroying an AI session on panel switch / route change

prepareSidePanel() force-cancelled an in-flight AI generation or
un-applied draft with no confirmation whenever comments or QA were
opened; the audits/edit/index.vue $route.path watcher did the same on
in-audit navigation. Only the beforeRouteLeave/beforeRouteUpdate
guards on the leaf pages (edit.js, sections.js) already confirmed.

Reuse the existing confirmLeaveIfAiGenerating composable:
- prepareSidePanel now takes a callback and runs it via
  runAfterAiGenerationCheck, so opening comments/QA confirms first
  when there's an active/generating AI session and proceeds silently
  otherwise. toggleCommentView/toggleQaView move their panel-opening
  logic into that callback.
- Replace the reactive $route.path watcher on audits/edit/index.vue
  (which fired after the route had already changed) with proper
  beforeRouteUpdate/beforeRouteLeave guards using
  confirmRouterLeaveIfAiGenerating, so navigation is actually blocked
  until confirmed instead of just cleaning up after the fact.

Show the AI QA summary in the results panel

The report summary was already stored by both the audit-qa store and
vulnerability-qa-panel, but never rendered or even wired through as a
prop. Add a summary prop to qa-results-panel.vue, rendered under the
stat tiles, and thread it through audit-qa-sidebar (store state) and
vulnerability-qa-panel (previously missing "summary" from its data(),
so it wasn't reactive there either).

Add regression coverage for HTML draft preview rendering

formatDraftPreview already sanitizes HTML drafts through the
allowlist sanitizer (Utils.htmlEncode) and the template already
renders the result via v-html, so formatted content (not escaped
source) was already showing correctly — no source change needed.
Add unit tests locking this in for html/array/text output types and
verifying disallowed tags (e.g. <script>) are stripped, since there
was no prior coverage for ai-chat-drawer.vue at all.

Add info severity filter tile and surface failed AI runs

Issue counts already included info severity, but the stat tiles only
offered error/warning/total, so info-only results (like a skipped AI
run) were invisible unless you dug into the issue list. Add a 4th
"Notes" stat tile that filters to severity: info, matching the
existing error/warning/total pattern.

"AI review skipped" / "AI duplicate review skipped" / "AI translation
link review skipped" issues were buried as ordinary info-severity rows
in whatever location group they landed in, making a failed AI run easy
to miss. Add splitAiUnavailableIssues/isAiUnavailableIssue to
qa-display.js and use them in audit-qa-sidebar.vue and
vulnerability-qa-panel.vue to pull these out of the normal issue list
and promote them to a dedicated banner in qa-results-panel.vue instead.

Add dark mode support to the QA results panel and AI chat drawer

.qa-run-meta, .qa-stat, .qa-summary, .qa-group__header, and
.ai-chat-context all had hardcoded light-mode colors (#fafafa, #f5f5f5,
#424242, etc.) with no dark-mode override, so they stayed light in an
otherwise dark UI. The panels' Quasar utility classes (bg-grey-3,
bg-grey-11, bg-blue-grey-1) are already handled by the app's global
dark-mode-colors() mixin in quasar.variables.scss — only these
component-local custom classes needed fixing.

Since .body--dark overrides don't match from inside a scoped style
block (the ancestor selector never carries the component's scope
hash — confirmed by grepping the codebase, where the only other
.body--dark usage lives in an unscoped block), add a second unscoped
<style> block to each component with just the dark-mode overrides,
matching that existing pattern. Verified with a production build that
the rules survive into the compiled CSS bundle unscoped as expected.

Add a "Test connection" button for AI providers

Misconfiguration (bad key/base URL/model) previously surfaced only as
a failed generation mid-workflow. Add POST /api/ai/test, mirroring the
LanguageTool test-connection pattern: it runs a minimal ping
completion against the resolved provider config and reports success
(with the responding model) or a clear error.

testProviderConnection in ai-client.js reuses the existing
resolveProviderConfig/buildLlmConfig/mapLlmError helpers rather than
duplicating provider-resolution logic. The route accepts per-provider
field overrides so a user can test with values just typed in the form
without saving first; masked-secret sentinels fall back to the stored
value, same convention as the regular settings save path.

Add a "Test connection" button under each provider's fields in
ai-provider-settings.vue with an inline success/failure message.

Move admin AI surfaces to i18n and fix naming

The entire admin AI UI (Assisted Writing / Quality Assurance pages,
the AI Integration settings card, ai-provider-settings.vue, and the
Data-menu entries) was hardcoded English with no i18n coverage, so
fr/de/pt/zh users saw raw English even outside the AI chat drawer
(which already had keys). Move all of it to a new `aiIntegration` i18n
namespace, authoritative in en-US with English-copy fallbacks added to
the other four locales, matching how several other namespaces already
degrade in this codebase.

QA_CHECK_OPTIONS and PROMPT_FIELD_SECTIONS previously baked label/
description strings into module-level constants evaluated once at
import time; since locale switching in this app is live (no reload),
that would have frozen these labels in whatever locale was active at
first load. Rebuilt them as computed properties that call $t() at
render time so they react to locale changes like the rest of the page.

Renames: "Programmatical Checks" -> "Programmatic Checks" (also fixed
the same typo on the QA results panel's run button) and "Redaction
Guidelines" -> "Writing Guidelines" for user-facing labels, including
the backend system-prompt wording sent to the AI and its validation
error message. The internal `redactionGuidelines` schema/variable name
and `ai:redaction-guidelines:*` permission scopes are unchanged.

Offer discard-and-start when starting AI on a field with an active session

Starting AI generation on a second field while another field's AI
drawer was open just showed a warning notify and aborted, forcing the
user to manually close the drawer and click again. Replace that with
a one-click confirm dialog offering to discard the current session and
start the new one, reusing runAfterAiGenerationCheck from the 2.5 fix
(same cancel-then-proceed mechanism, session state has something to
lose in this branch by construction so it always confirms).

Extend confirmLeaveIfAiGenerating.js to accept optional dialog text
overrides so this call site can use the already-defined-but-unused
aiChat.discardAiSessionTitle/Message keys and a new "Discard & start
new" button label, instead of the generic "Leave/Stay" wording used
by the route-guard and panel-switch call sites.

generateFieldDraftAI's post-conflict-check body is extracted into
runFieldDraftGeneration so it can run either immediately (no
conflict) or from the dialog's confirm callback (conflict).

Standardize AI (sparkle) button placement across editor surfaces

The AI entry point looked different in each of the three places it
appears: mid-toolbar between caption and undo in the rich editor
(styled like an ordinary format button), alone on its own grey bar in
textarea-array, and appended inline without emphasis in custom-fields.

Standardize on: pushed to the far right of the toolbar/bar (via
q-space in Editor.vue, justify-end in textarea-array.vue) and colored
primary so it reads as "the AI entry point" rather than another format
button. custom-fields.vue's six field-type AI buttons were already in
the append slot (right-aligned); they only needed the primary color
for visual consistency with the other two.

De-dupe repeated provider validation and route-leave helpers

backend/src/routes/ai.js repeated the same "resolve provider from
request/settings default, validate against AI_PROVIDERS" block 3
times across handleAiGenerate, handleAiQa, and handleVulnerabilityQa.
Extract resolveProvider(req, settings), returning the resolved
provider or null, and have each handler check for null.

frontend edit.js's continueRouteLeave and continueRouteUpdate were
byte-identical (unsaved-changes / highlight-warning confirm dialogs
before continuing navigation). Collapse to one continueRoute method
called by both beforeRouteLeave and beforeRouteUpdate.

Don't load the entire vulnerability database for single/loadOnly QA

handleVulnerabilityQa called Vulnerability.getAll() unconditionally at
the top of the handler, even for "load the cached report for one
template" and "load a draft's (nonexistent) report" requests that
don't need the rest of the database at all.

Move the fetch down: loadOnly + vulnerabilityId now fetches just that
document via Vulnerability.findById; loadOnly + a draft vulnerability
needs no database read at all (it can never have a stored report).
Only the "all templates" paths (loadOnly or not) and the two AI-run
paths that do cross-template duplicate detection still load everything,
since they genuinely need it.

Also drop an unused `mode` variable left over from an earlier version
of this handler (every call site already passes its own literal
mode: 'single'/'all').
Update translations and styles for QA components; standardize 'Infos' label
Enhance AI field handling and HTML normalization; add context scoping for field values
Move diff preview in the chat sidebar and add translations
Improve AI chat session management

Enforce ai-settings:read/update server-side for AI provider config

The `ai-settings:read/update` scopes only gated the provider card in the
UI; the actual read/write went through GET/PUT /api/settings enforced by
`settings:read`/`settings:update`. As a result a `settings:update` user
could change providers/keys regardless of the AI scopes, while an
`ai-settings:update`-only user saw editable fields that 403'd on save.

Split the AI provider subtree (ai.private.*, ai.public.enabled,
ai.public.defaultProvider) onto a dedicated endpoint pair:

- GET/PUT /api/settings/ai enforce ai-settings:read / ai-settings:update
- GET /api/settings strips the provider subtree for callers without
  ai-settings:read
- PUT /api/settings restores the provider subtree for callers without
  ai-settings:update, so it can never change providers/keys there
- POST /api/ai/test now requires ai-settings:update (was settings:update)

Frontend: the settings page saves the provider subtree through the
dedicated endpoint when the user has ai-settings:update but not
settings:update, and the Save button renders for that persona (while
Revert/Import/Export stay gated on settings:update).

Adds a backend role test proving both scope directions and confirming
generic-endpoint protection, plus frontend service/page coverage.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Close SSRF DNS-rebinding gap in QA reference link checker

Validation resolved the hostname and checked the returned IPs, then
`fetch` resolved the hostname again independently for the actual
connection. A DNS-rebinding host could answer with a public IP during
validation and an internal IP (metadata endpoint, 10.x, 127.0.0.1, …)
for the connection, so a malicious finding reference could reach
internal services despite passing validation.

Pin the outbound request to the exact address that passed validation:
`resolveValidatedAddress` now returns the vetted { address, family }, and
`performPinnedRequest` connects through the built-in http/https modules
with a custom `lookup` that always yields that address. The URL hostname
is preserved for TLS SNI / Host, so certificate validation is unaffected.
Every redirect hop is re-resolved, re-validated and re-pinned.

Also block 100.64.0.0/10 (CGNAT / shared address space), which is
commonly used for cloud-internal ranges.

Tests mock the http/https layer instead of fetch and add coverage for a
hostname resolving to CGNAT, the pinned-address wiring, and CGNAT literals.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Store-keyed QA run state with in-progress indicator and double-run guard

QA run state lived in component data / the audit-qa store's report fields,
so closing the drawer, switching a vulnerability language tab (which
remounts the panel via :key), or reopening the run-all dialog destroyed
an in-flight run. `auditQa.open()` also unconditionally reloaded the
cached report, overwriting a running review with stale results and
re-enabling the run buttons with no "generating" signal — and nothing
stopped a second concurrent run.

Introduce a shared `qa-runs` store keyed by target (audit:<id>,
vuln:<id>:<locale>, all:<locale>, draft) holding { running, startedAt,
report, error }:

- `start` guards against a second run for a target already running and
  keeps the previous report visible while running.
- `load` re-attaches to an in-flight run instead of restarting it, and a
  slow cached fetch can't clobber a run that began during the fetch.
- audit-qa and vulnerability-qa-panel derive their view state from the
  store; the panel survives close/reopen, tab switches and route changes.
  An unsaved vulnerability uses a single `draft` key so its results
  survive language-tab switches, and is reset when the modal closes.

qa-results-panel shows a top progress bar and an "AI QA in progress…
started {time}" line, dims the previous report, and disables run buttons
while running. A pulsing dot on each QA toolbar button (findings /
sections / general pages and the vulnerability modal) signals an in-flight
run even when the panel is closed.

Adds a qa-runs store test suite (guard, re-attach, load race, error,
reset) and panel running-indicator tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

regardless of the AI scopes, while an ai-settings:update-only user saw
editable fields that would 403 on save. There was never a real second
tier of access underneath the two extra scopes.

Drop ai-settings:read/update from the permissions catalog and gate the
provider card and its edit control on the same settings:read/update the
rest of the settings page already uses, removing canEditAiSettings as a
separate concept. AI provider config now behaves like every other
section on this page — one card, one permission pair, no illusion of
independent granularity.

role.test.js now asserts the two scopes are absent from the settings
permission group instead of present.

runAiDuplicateChecks and runAiUnlinkedTranslationChecks sent the entire
template catalog to the provider in one request for "all templates" runs,
so a mature vulnerability database could exceed the model's context limit.
Split the catalog into overlapping batches (40 templates, 5 overlap) so
boundary duplicates still land in a shared batch, and merge/dedupe issues
across batches. Single-target runs batch the candidate list without
overlap since the target anchors every comparison.

Fix QA issue navigation (go to field)

Field highlighting was gated on commentMode, so QA navigation set
fieldHighlighted but nothing ever lit up. QA "go to field" also never
switched tabs and matched findings by title, so duplicate-titled findings
always routed to the first match and renamed findings fell through to
/general.

- Decouple the highlighted-border styling from commentMode: it now also
  triggers when the QA drawer is open, in both the finding editor and
  custom-fields (which needed a new qaDrawerOpen prop).

  the same field-to-tab mapping comments already use) and scroll it into
  view, on both the findings and general pages.
- Carry the finding _id in QA issue locations (finding:<id>::<title>) so
  navigation matches by id instead of by title, falling back to title only
  when no id is present or it no longer resolves. AI-produced issues only
  know titles, so a location is only backfilled with an id when the title
  is unambiguous in the audit.

  unhandled) and fix the toolbar separator being hidden outside edit mode.

Make the Assisted Writing prompts page usable with many custom fields

Every finding custom field rendered as a full-width, always-expanded card
with a tall autogrow textarea and a dev-facing caption ("Entity: finding |
Field key: custom-field:<id> | Output: html"), so a library with 25+
custom fields was a wall of identical-looking cards.

- Collapse each field to a one-line row (toggle, label, output-type chip)
  using a per-field q-expansion-item; the prompt textarea only renders
  once expanded.
- Add a filter box that searches field labels across all groups and
  auto-expands matching groups.
- Strip the redundant "Finding/Section Custom Field: " prefix from the
  row label now that the group header already says "Custom fields".
- Sticky save bar with a live unsaved-change count, plus a
  beforeRouteLeave guard so navigating away with unsaved prompt,
  guideline, or QA changes prompts a confirm (this page previously
  discarded silently, unlike every other PwnDoc editor).
- savePrompts() used to silently drop global prompts with only a label or
  only a prompt body; it now blocks the save and flags the incomplete
  entry instead of losing it.

Add a Stop control to the AI chat drawer

Generation was a single blocking request with a spinner; the only way to
back out was the "close while generating" confirm, which abandoned the UI
but left the request running and could later write a stale response into
whatever session/conversation happened to be open by the time it resolved.

- Send AI generation requests with an axios CancelToken; while a request
  is in flight the send button becomes a Stop button that cancels it.
- Cancelling restores the input and rolls back the pending user message
  with no error toast (a user-initiated stop isn't a failure); a real
  request failure still shows one.
- Guard the response/catch/finally handlers with the session id captured
  at request time so a cancelled or slow response can never mutate a
  conversation that has since moved on to a different session.
- "Close while generating" now also cancels the in-flight request instead
  of just resetting local state.
- Fix boot/axios.js's response interceptor, which unconditionally read
  error.response.status: a cancelled or network-level (no response)
  error would throw inside the interceptor itself instead of surfacing
  a clean, catchable error.

Fix "run all" vulnerability QA misrouted into the draft/single path

normalizeDraftVulnerability(raw = {}) defaulted its argument to {} when
called with undefined. A "run all" request sends no vulnerability key at
all, so req.body.vulnerability was undefined and the default kicked in,
producing a truthy synthetic draft object instead of null.

That made every "run all" request take the single/draft branch instead
of the all-templates one: loadOnly returned an empty single-mode
response instead of the cached all-templates report, and an actual run
called getVulnerabilityDetail on a draft object with no `details` array,
which returned null and surfaced as "Draft vulnerability has no content
for this language" instead of ever calling runAllVulnerabilitiesQa.

Drop the default parameter so undefined correctly falls through to the
existing !raw check and returns null.

Fix AI request timeouts with SSE streaming and background QA jobs

Long-running AI provider calls were being killed by the proxy's idle read
timeout while the HTTP connection sat open waiting for a slow response.

Address it on three fronts:

- /api/ai/generate now streams its response over SSE, emitting a heartbeat
  on every LLM chunk so the proxy's idle timer never fires mid-generation.
  The draft/reply contract is unchanged; only the transport differs. The
  frontend consumes it via fetch()+ReadableStream and acts on the terminal
  done/error event.
- Audit QA and single-vulnerability QA move their LLM call to a detached
  background job (ai-qa-single-job.js) so the request returns immediately
  and the client loads the persisted report via loadOnly or the
  audit-qa:done / vuln-qa-single:done socket events. Programmatic-only
  scope has no LLM call and still resolves inline.
- nginx: scope proxy_buffering off + 300s read/send timeouts to a dedicated
  location = /api/ai/generate block instead of applying them to all of /api/,
  so normal API calls keep default buffering and timeouts.

Also raise the default per-provider timeout from 30s to 120s, add a timedOut
i18n string (all locales), and cover the streaming and background-job paths
with backend and frontend unit tests.

actually cached anything. It also wouldn't pay off here: the guideline
blocks are small and AI calls are sparse and human-triggered, so prompt
caching's savings (amortizing a large static prefix across frequent
repeat requests) don't apply. Reduce redactionGuidelines and
qaInstructions to plain inline { content } blocks;
